extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and authors preparing submissions to The American Mathematical Monthly (articles, notes, problems, reviews, Mathbits, letters)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for preparing and submitting manuscripts to The American Mathematical Monthly, covering acceptable article types, formatting, style, file requirements, ethical and data-sharing policies, and production/charges information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal only publishes manuscripts in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double anonymous review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal has a double anonymous review policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have shared an earlier version on a preprint server, anonymity cannot be guaranteed; see preprints policy and citation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable types of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Mathematical Monthly accepts Articles, Notes, Problems and Solutions, Book Reviews, Mathbits, and Letters to the Editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each type has different expectations (e.g., Articles 6–20 pages; Notes short and sharply focused; Mathbits ≤1 page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposition and broad appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly prioritizes articles that are clear, informative, engaging and accessible to a broad audience; exposition and broad appeal are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate figures, diagrams, and photographs are encouraged; excessive notation in abstracts or titles is discouraged because it limits broad readership and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Should contain an unstructured abstract of 250 words with limited use of mathematical notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts should entice readers and make clear why the paper is interesting and important; highlight concepts rather than summarize technical mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Should contain no more than 5 keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See guidance on making your article more discoverable for title and SEO recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article length
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles generally range from 6–20 pages in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly articles are meant to be read and discussed, not just archived; page guidance helps match the journal's style and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes format and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes are short, sharply focused, and may be informal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often provide a new proof, novel presentation, or lively discussion of a single issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathbits length
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathbits are 1 page in length or less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should provide appropriate 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification terms for their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide at least one and up to three 5-digit MSC classifications that best describe your paper (links to MSC provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author details on cover page
rubrics_metrics.description: All listed authors should include full name and affiliation on the cover page; one author identified as corresponding author with email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where available include ORCiDs and social media handles. Affiliations are those where the research was conducted. If co-authors move during review, new affiliation can be a footnote. No affiliation changes after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes on contributors (author bios)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply a short biographical note (2 to 5 sentences) for each author on original articles only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes and reviews do not run author bios; include affiliations and email addresses for notes and reviews instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting proposed problems or solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem proposals must be accompanied by solutions and should not be under consideration elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit problems/solutions via the specified Submittable link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image descriptions (alt text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add image descriptions (alternative text) for images conveying information necessary for understanding the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taylor & Francis may produce image descriptions with AI; authors can include their own and will have opportunity to review AI-generated descriptions during proofing. Follow provided guidelines when supplying alt text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling and quotation style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use American spelling consistently; use double quotation marks except where a quotation is within a quotation (then use single quotes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long quotations should be indented without quotation marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided templates and style file
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should use the updated Monthly template and style file with no custom formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates (article/note, cover letter, MathBits) and style file (maa-monthly.sty) included in Monthly_Templates.zip. Contact journal if unable to use template. Updated template includes a BibTeX bst file.

rubrics_metrics.name: File submission requirements (LaTeX and Word)
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitting in LaTeX, convert files to PDF beforehand; upload the PDF as the 'Manuscript - with author details'/'Manuscript - anonymous' file and upload LaTeX source files as a single zip file alongside submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission Portal manages files across Taylor & Francis journals. Ensure equations are editable if submitting Word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference style
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the NLM style of references; a bst file for BibTeX users is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the reference guide linked in instructions to prepare references correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures quality and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be high quality: 1200 dpi for line art, 600 dpi for grayscale and 300 dpi for color, at the correct size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred file formats: PS, PDF, JPEG, TIFF, or Microsoft Word (DOC/DOCX) for figures drawn in Word. See 'Submission of electronic artwork' for other file types. Supply editable files where appropriate. Color reproduced online free; print color charges apply (pricing and thresholds specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should present new information rather than duplicating text and should be interpretable without reference to the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply tables as editable files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations in Word submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitting as a Word document, ensure that equations are editable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See linked guidance on mathematical symbols and equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SI units (non-italicized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using third-party material and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must obtain necessary permission to reuse third-party material not covered by informal fair-use allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short extracts of text and some other material may be permitted for criticism/review without permission; otherwise obtain written permission prior to submission. Link provided for requesting permission guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality checks and submission agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting your paper you agree to originality checks; the journal uses Crossref to screen papers for unoriginal material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality checks occur during peer-review and production. If a paper is rejected, wait three months before resubmission to the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission delay after rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is rejected, authors should wait three months before submitting another paper to the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing policy and data availability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal applies the Taylor & Francis Basic Data Sharing Policy: authors are encouraged to share or make open the data supporting their paper and to provide a Data Availability Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At submission you will be asked if a data set is associated; if yes provide DOI, pre-reserved DOI, hyperlink, or other persistent identifier. Authors encouraged to deposit data in recognized repositories that mint persistent identifiers (preferably DOIs). Datasets associated with a manuscript are not formally peer reviewed; authors are responsible for data soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition timing and identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you choose to share data, deposit data in a recognized repository prior to or at time of submission and provide the DOI or other persistent identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If providing a pre-registered DOI be prepared to share reviewer URL associated with the deposit upon request by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental online material
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental material (video, fileset, audio, etc.) can be published online via Figshare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental material should support and be pertinent to the paper. Guidance and submission process linked; Taylor & Francis Editing Services can assist with creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding statement wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide funding details in specified formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates given: single agency — 'This work was supported by the [Funding Agency] under Grant [number xxxx].' For multiple agencies list each agency and grant number separated by semicolons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure (conflict of interest) statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge any financial or non-financial interests arising from direct applications of research; if none, state this explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The authors report there are no competing interests to declare.' Link provided for further guidance on what constitutes a conflict and how to disclose it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and open access options
rubrics_metrics.description: Taylor & Francis offers a number of license and reuse options, including Creative Commons licenses when publishing open access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read more on publishing agreements to choose appropriate copyright option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication charges and color figure charges
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no submission fees, publication fees, or page charges for this journal. Color figures reproduced online are free; print color incurs charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print color charges: $400 per figure for first four color figures; figures 5+ charged at $75 per figure (regional currency equivalents given). Open Select open-access requires an APC payable by corresponding author (use APC finder for amount).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria and checklist items
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all listed authors meet Taylor & Francis authorship criteria and include required author details on the cover page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items include author details, funding details, disclosure statement, data availability statement where applicable, and templates for contributor notes. One author must be identified as corresponding author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance and archiving
rubrics_metrics.description: On acceptance, keep a copy of your Accepted Manuscript; find out more about sharing your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: My Authored Works provides metrics and a free eprints link for sharing. Article reprints and ordering information provided post-acceptance.
